title: A is for ANGLE OF ATTACK: The single most critical principle that saves your landings | MSFS A-Z
description:
Whether you are floating all the way down a short runway in Microsoft Flight Simulator, smashing the nose gear down, or wondering why the stall horn is suddenly screaming at you during a steep turn, the culprit isn't your airspeed. It's your angle of attack. If you have ever assumed angle of attack is just a fancy word for pitch, this video is going to completely change how you fly your approaches. That confusion stops today.

In the premier episode of Cycle 2 of our Microsoft Flight Simulator A-Z series, we are tackling the fundamental building block of flight: the letter A. We break down the core aerodynamic differences between where your nose points and where your aircraft is actually going, bust the ultimate aviation pitch myth using a simple car window analogy, and take a complete cockpit tour to find these critical indicators across GA planes, airliners, and military jets. Finally, we walk through step-by-step guides to unlock hidden AOA displays in your favorite high-fidelity add-ons.

In this video, you’ll discover:

- The Core Theory of AOA: Why your wing slices through oncoming airflow independent of pitch, and how to visualize the chord line vs. relative wind.
- Systems & Indicators Showcase: How to read angle of attack variations across the Garmin G1000, Boeing 737 HUD/PFD tapes, Airbus fly-by-wire limits, and Navy indexer boxes.
- Pro-Tip: PMDG 737 Configuration: Exactly how to navigate the FMC aircraft options and display settings to manually turn on your missing digital dial.
- Demo - Slow Flight & Vision Jet Setup: Unlocking the Garmin G3000 PFD settings to switch the AOA indicator from "Auto" to "On" over the Netherlands.
- Demo - The Critical Limit: Pushing a fly-by-wire system to its absolute limits in the F/A-18 Hornet to observe aerodynamic shake and recovery.

Understanding the difference between raw airspeed and aerodynamic load separates casual simmers from real-world virtual pilots. Next time you drop onto final approach, track your flight path vector, check your wing limits, and manage your AOA like a professional.

Welcome to Cycle 2!
We are officially kicking off a brand-new journey through the aviation alphabet! Thank you for flying along as we refine our skills.
